analysis.title: Salesforce Inc Partner Sentiment Tracker: Third-Party Surveys Point to AI Adoption Hitting Real-World Challenges, Even Though Disruption Risk Is Limited
key_insights: Across 10 partner and customer channel checks, JPMorgan concludes disruption risk to Salesforce's core systems is limited, but Agentforce adoption and monetization face real-world hurdles.

Three main challenges: enterprise data readiness slowing AI deployments (while supporting Data 360 demand in complex use cases), difficulty showing broad repeatable ROI beyond service implementations, and customers seeking seat reductions while taking on new AI and data spending commitments.
The seat-to-consumption transition may create a timing gap between pressure on seat-based revenue and the ramp in consumption-based revenue, which partners say may take 12-18 months to ramp.

Agentforce production maturity is uneven. Some integrators report 30%-60% of clients or projects in production, but cohorts and definitions differ, and other checks show many live agents have limited daily usage or sit in isolated workflows.

One IT services VP said 30%-35% of clients were live with another 10%-15% in proof of concept. A digital consultancy director said fewer than a dozen of about four dozen built agents remained in active daily use.

Data and organizational readiness constrain Agentforce scaling more than the AI models do. A global IT services lead estimated 80%-90% of projects need substantial data cleanup, and a consulting executive called the challenge 30% technology and 70% people and process.

Flex Credits lower the cost of experimentation, but CFOs are uncomfortable replacing predictable seat costs with uncapped consumption, and customers lack usage history to forecast credit and data consumption.
Selected service deployments delivered 20%-35% contact deflection and 15%-25% reductions in handling time, but broad enterprise ROI remains hard to establish.

Partner growth is positive but dispersed. One IT services VP reported 25% y/y growth, deal closures up about 30% and renewal spending up 10%-15%, while a digital consultancy described Salesforce-only revenue as flat.
About one-quarter of renewals at one global IT services firm involved requests for 5%-10% seat reductions. Agentforce and Data 360 attach could still support 5%-10% net TCV expansion in those deals.

Headless adoption through Slack, Teams and custom interfaces expands Salesforce's back-end role but may weaken the link between workflow usage and dedicated CRM seats. The checks do not establish broad seat cannibalization.

Data 360 and Informatica strengthen the data proposition, but customers want to keep Snowflake or Databricks as their primary data foundation. A group CIO at an energy conglomerate prioritizes Databricks and is only selectively evaluating Agentforce.

Partner economics face pressure from Salesforce Professional Services and AI-assisted delivery. Agentic and headless engagements can reach 8,000-15,000 hours versus 600-2,000 hours for conventional implementations, so the services opportunity is shifting rather than contracting.

The core CRM installed base is defensible given embedded data, custom workflows and switching costs. The risk is leakage of incremental AI, data, workflow and engagement spending to Microsoft, HubSpot, ServiceNow and independent data platforms, with more open competition in greenfield deals.

market_movers.rationale: Rating and coverage are unchanged. The report is a channel-check tracker and states no price target. Price was $214.83 on 16 Nov 2026.

sector_views.rationale: Not a sector call. The report supports Salesforce's core CRM durability while flagging slower AI monetization and share competition for incremental spending.

risk_factors: Enterprise data readiness slows Agentforce deployments and monetization.
Customers struggle to establish repeatable ROI beyond service-oriented use cases.
Seat reductions may arrive before consumption revenue ramps, which could take 12-18 months.
CFO resistance to uncapped consumption pricing and difficulty forecasting credit and data usage.
Headless adoption may decouple workflow usage from dedicated Salesforce seats.
Microsoft, HubSpot, ServiceNow and independent data platforms may capture more new AI, data and workflow spending.
Customers want to preserve independent data foundations such as Snowflake and Databricks, which limits Data 360 lock-in.
Salesforce Professional Services is competing with partners for implementation and managed-services work.

tension_points.bull_case: Agentforce is moving into production, successful deployments generate follow-on work, and Agentforce and Data 360 attach could support 5%-10% net TCV expansion in seat-reduction renewals. Core CRM remains durable.
tension_points.bear_case: Data readiness, unproven ROI and CFO resistance to uncapped consumption slow adoption. Seat reductions may precede the consumption ramp by 12-18 months, and competitors may capture incremental spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Consumption revenue taking longer than 12-18 months to ramp while about one-quarter of renewals continue to request 5%-10% seat reductions.

theme_stances.key_argument: AI demand is real, but the monetization curve is more gradual than customer interest suggests.
theme_stances.evidence: AI demand is real, but the monetization curve appears more gradual

theme_stances.key_argument: Embedded data, customized workflows and high switching costs protect existing enterprise deployments.
theme_stances.evidence: The core CRM franchise remains durable
